questions.prompt: How do `Rc<T>` and `Arc<T>` differ?

options.text: `Arc<T>` uses atomic reference counting (thread-safe, implements `Send + Sync` if `T` does); `Rc<T>` is single-threaded

questions.prompt: What is interior mutability (`RefCell<T>`, `Mutex<T>`) used for in Rust?

options.text: Mutating inner data through a shared `&T` reference by enforcing borrowing/locking rules dynamically at runtime

questions.prompt: What happens if two `RefCell` borrows overlap mutably (`let a = cell.borrow(); let b = cell.borrow_mut();`)?

options.text: Runtime `panic!` because `RefCell` enforces Rust's aliasing XOR mutability rule dynamically

code.source:
let a = cell.borrow();
let b = cell.borrow_mut(); // panics

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `Send` and `Sync` in Rust. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `T: Sync` means `&T` can be safely shared across threads (`&T: Send`)
`Rc<T>` is neither `Send` nor `Sync` because its refcount is non-atomic
`Mutex<T>` requires `T` to be `Sync` even for exclusive locking
`T: Send` means ownership of `T` can be transferred across threads

questions.prompt: Match each smart pointer / synchronization primitive to its use case.

columns.label: Single-owner heap allocation (recursive types, trait objects)
Shared mutable state across multiple threads

questions.prompt: What is the critical danger of holding a `std::sync::MutexGuard` across an `.await` point in `async` Rust?

options.text: The task may yield while holding the OS mutex, starving/deadlocking other tasks on the executor thread (use `tokio::sync::Mutex` or drop the guard before `.await`)

questions.prompt: Why do Rust `async fn` Futures do nothing until `.await`ed or polled by an executor?

options.text: Rust Futures are lazy state machines; they only advance when polled

questions.prompt: What does `Pin<&mut T>` guarantee for self-referential `async` state machines?

options.text: The value `T` will not be moved in memory (unless `T: Unpin`), keeping internal self-references valid

questions.prompt: What is `Cow<'a, str>` (`std::borrow::Cow`) used for?

options.text: Clone-on-write: holding a borrowed `&'a str` when no mutation is needed and allocating an owned `String` only if modification is required

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the 5 superpowers unlocked inside an `unsafe { ... }` block?

options.text: Bypassing the borrow checker for safe `&mut T` references

questions.prompt: Why should `unsafe` code in a library be encapsulated behind a small, well-documented safe wrapper?

options.text: So callers can rely on the safe API without upholding manual memory invariants, and audits focus on a small `// SAFETY:` surface

questions.prompt: What tool in the Rust ecosystem executes tests under an interpreter to detect Undefined Behavior in `unsafe` code (like Stacked Borrows / Tree Borrows violations)?
What happens if a `Mutex` is poisoned in Rust (a thread panics while holding the lock)?

options.text: `mutex.lock()` returns `Err(PoisonError)` alerting callers that protected data may be in an inconsistent state

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Rust FFI (`extern "C"`) with C libraries. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Structs shared across FFI should be marked `#[repr(C)]` for predictable C field layout
Functions exported to C use `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn ...`
Panicking across an `extern "C"` FFI boundary is Undefined Behavior (use `std::panic::catch_unwind` or return error codes)
Rust `String` has the exact same ABI layout as C `char *`

questions.prompt: What does `#[non_exhaustive]` on a public `enum` or `struct` communicate to downstream crates?

options.text: Future minor versions may add variants/fields, forcing external crates to include a `_ => ...` wildcard arm or use constructors

questions.prompt: What is a zero-sized type (ZST) in Rust (like `()` or `struct Marker;`)?

options.text: A type that causes a compile error
A type with `size_of::<T>() == 0` that compiles away to zero runtime bytes while still enforcing compile-time type/state checks (typestate pattern)

questions.prompt: What does `PhantomData<T>` express in a generic struct that doesn't store a field of type `T`?

options.text: Tells the compiler about logical ownership, variance, or drop-check relationships with `T` without occupying runtime bytes

questions.prompt: Why can `std::mem::transmute` be dangerous even when `size_of::<A>() == size_of::<B>()`?

options.text: It bypasses validity invariants (e.g., creating an invalid `bool`, non-UTF-8 `str`, or misaligned/dangling reference), causing immediate UB

questions.prompt: What is `MaybeUninit<T>` used for in low-level Rust?

options.text: Safely working with uninitialized memory buffers before calling `.assume_init()` once fully initialized

questions.prompt: Match each Rust concurrency tool to its primary strength.

columns.label: Multi-producer, single-consumer message passing between threads
Allows many concurrent readers OR one exclusive writer

questions.prompt: What does `Ordering::Acquire` / `Ordering::Release` on atomics guarantee compared to `Ordering::Relaxed`?

options.text: Zero CPU fences on all architectures
Global total order across all variables
Synchronizes-with relationship: writes before a `Release` store become visible to another thread after a matching `Acquire` load

questions.prompt: What is monomorphization bloat in generic Rust code, and how do you mitigate it?

options.text: Generating separate machine code for each concrete `T` in large generic functions; mitigate by factoring non-generic inner helpers (polymorphization) or using `&dyn Trait`

questions.prompt: What does `std::thread::scope(|s| { ... })` enable that `std::thread::spawn` does not?

options.text: Spawning threads that borrow non-`'static` local stack variables because the scope guarantees all threads join before returning

questions.prompt: What does `#[inline]` in a library crate allow across crate boundaries?

options.text: Allows downstream crates to inline the function body during compilation (useful for small hot helpers)

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for designing idiomatic error handling in Rust crates. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Panic inside library functions whenever an input file is missing
Use concrete, structured error enums (e.g., via `thiserror`) in library crates so callers can match variants
Use contextual error types (e.g., `anyhow::Result`) in binaries/CLIs where callers mainly log/propagate
Implement `std::error::Error`, `Display`, and `Debug` on public error types

questions.prompt: What is `Deref` coercion used for, and why should you NOT abuse `Deref` to fake OOP inheritance?

options.text: `Deref` is intended for smart pointers (`Box`, `Rc`, `String` -> `str`); abusing it for inheritance surprises callers with implicit conversions and method resolution ambiguity

questions.prompt: What does `std::hint::black_box(x)` do in Rust microbenchmarks?

options.text: Prevents the optimizer from constant-folding or eliminating dead computations during benchmarking

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Cargo feature flags (`[features]`) and why should features be additive?

options.text: Cargo unifies features across the dependency graph—if one crate enables a feature and another expects it disabled, non-additive features break builds

questions.prompt: What does `Pin::new(&mut val)` require on `val`'s type?

options.text: `val: Unpin` (types that are safe to move even when pinned, which includes most ordinary types)

questions.prompt: What does `std::pin::pin!(fut)` (stabilized in Rust 1.68) allow?

options.text: Pins a `!Unpin` future directly on the local stack without a `Box::pin` heap allocation

questions.prompt: Why is `HashMap` in `std::collections` seeded with a random SipHash state by default?

options.text: To protect against HashDoS (hash-collision denial-of-service) attacks on untrusted keys

questions.prompt: What does `#[must_use]` on a custom type or function do?

options.text: Emits a compiler warning if a caller ignores the returned value

questions.prompt: Match each Rust cast/conversion mechanism to its safety level.

columns.label: Truncating/wrapping numeric cast (lossy if out of range)
`unsafe` bit-level reinterpretation; UB if target invariants violated

questions.prompt: What does `cargo audit` (or `cargo-deny`) check in production Rust pipelines?

options.text: Known security advisories (RustSec), license compliance, and duplicate dependencies in `Cargo.lock`

questions.prompt: What is a common pitfall when implementing `PartialOrd` and `Ord` manually?

options.text: Inconsistency between `PartialEq` (`==`) and `Ord` (`Ordering::Equal`) breaks `BTreeMap` and `BinaryHeap` invariants

questions.prompt: What does `split_at_mut(mid)` on a slice `&mut [T]` solve?

options.text: Borrowing two disjoint mutable sub-slices `&mut [T]` simultaneously without violating the single-`&mut` rule

questions.prompt: Select all ways to reduce heap allocations in hot Rust loops. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Pass slices `&[T]` / `&str` or `Cow<str>` instead of cloning `Vec`/`String`
Call `.clone()` inside inner loops on every item
Reuse buffers with `.clear()` or `String::clear()` across iterations

questions.prompt: What does `std::sync::OnceLock<T>` (stabilized in Rust 1.70) provide?

options.text: Thread-safe lazy one-time initialization of a global or static value without `unsafe` or external crates

questions.prompt: Why does Rust's `?` operator work seamlessly with custom error wrappers?

options.text: Because `?` desugars to calling `From::from(err)` on the error type

questions.prompt: What does `Arc::make_mut(&mut arc)` do?

options.text: Returns `&mut T` directly if `strong_count == 1 && weak_count == 0`, otherwise clones `T` into a new `Arc` (copy-on-write)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `async` cancellation in Rust. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Types holding state across `.await` must be careful about cancellation safety (e.g., partial reads/writes)
In `tokio::select!`, losing branches are dropped and cancelled
Dropping a `Future` automatically rolls back database transactions on remote servers without code
Dropping a `Future` before completion cancels it at its current `.await` point

questions.prompt: What is the role of `Send` in `async fn` traits or `tokio::spawn`?

options.text: Multi-threaded work-stealing executors can move a `Future` between OS threads across `.await` points, so all state held across `.await` must be `Send`
